chunks.title: What we do | Dean of Students
chunks.text:
## What we do

#### Start with us. We know Virginia Tech. Our caring team wants to get to know you so we can walk with you every step of the way. We are mentors and advocates who can point you in the right direction, be a sounding board, and assist with personal, social, and academic challenges. We're here to help—and cheer you on from orientation to graduation!

## General Support and Advice

Our staff is here to provide support and advice when life throws you a curve. If you are having difficulty in your personal or academic life, we are here to assist you in finding the appropriate resources to help. Quick answers to common concerns are below.

## Crisis and Emergency Response

Someone from our office is on call 24 hours a day, seven days a week. Additionally, staff from [Cook Counseling Center](https://ucc.vt.edu/) and [Housing](https://housing.vt.edu/) are also on call during the same hours.

In cases of emergency between the hours of 8 a.m. and 5 p.m., call 540-231-3787. After hours, the on-call staff member from the Dean's staff may be reached by calling the [Virginia Tech Police](https://police.vt.edu/) at 540-231-6411.

## Counsel and Referral

Our staff is trained to help you determine the appropriate course of action if you have a crisis, need medical care, or just need to talk. If you need services that we are unable to provide, we will refer you to professionals who can help.

## Student Conduct Referral Advising

Call the Dean's staff office at 231-3787 to schedule an appointment.

## Class Absence Verification

Your professors and/or supervisors ultimately decide whether or not you can make up missed classes, assignments, exams, employment, or other activities. If you provide proper documentation, the Dean of Students staff can verify your absence due to life events that are beyond the scope of your control, including:

- Illness or death of a family member or friend

- Off-campus medical appointments or hospital admission*

- Court subpoenas

- Military orders

- [Faith-based practices or celebrations](https://dos.vt.edu/interfaith/calendar.html)

The Dean of Students staff will not provide absence verifications for the following reasons:

- Family celebrations

- Planned events, such as vacations or trips abroad

- Internships, interviews, student organization trips, or academic trips

For absences due to these circumstances, you are encouraged to discuss the reason for absence with your professor and/or supervisor, who will use their discretion when deciding whether or not to allow makeup work.

chunks.title: What we do | Dean of Students
chunks.text:
## Class Absence Verification

The Dean of Students staff provides absence verification only. They do not "excuse" or "approve" absences. Faculty have the final decision on the completion of any missed assignments, tests, or other academic commitments. To submit a request please submit an absence verification request and a dean will be in touch.

chunks.title: Student Emergency Fund | Dean of Students
chunks.text:
## Student Emergency Fund

Through generous donations provided by many caring Hokies, the Dean of Students Office has been entrusted to manage a fund for students who find themselves in immediate financial need, due to no fault of their own. This means, any student currently enrolled at Virginia Tech can apply for a one-time grant to help during emergent circumstances.

If there are funds available through Financial Aid such as subsidized / unsubsidized loans or a Parent Plus loan, we will encourage these options be used. These funds are limited, so those experiencing the possibility of eviction or food insecurity will be given priority.

[Student Emergency Fund Contact Form](https://cm.maxient.com/reportingform.php?VirginiaTech&layout_id=19)

chunks.title: Resources for Students, Families, Faculty, and Staff | Dean of Students
chunks.text:
## Resources for Students, Families, Faculty, and Staff

- [Student Code of Conduct](https://codeofconduct.vt.edu/) – A guide covering the Code of Conduct, University Policies for Student Life, and other policies and procedures that students are required to know and abide.

- [Connections for Off-Campus Students](https://campuslife.vt.edu/secl_services/VTOCH.html) – Information on off-campus housing options for students, including listings, resources, and message boards.

- [Annual Notice on Rights and Responsibilities of the Virginia Tech Community.](https://news.vt.edu/articles/2023/09/hr-2023-annual-notice-rights-and-responsibilities.html)

- [Safe Zone](http://ccc.vt.edu/resources/safe_zone.html) – This program provides a more accepting environment for lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, and questioning students and their allies at Virginia Tech.

- [SAFE at VT](http://www.safe.vt.edu/) – Support and resources around the topic of sexual violence and sexual misconduct.

- [Threat Assessment](http://www.threatassessment.vt.edu/) – The purpose of the Threat Assessment Team is to determine if an individual poses, or may reasonably pose, a threat of violence to self, others, or the Virginia Tech community and to intervene to avert the thread and maintain the safety of the situation. Acts of intolerance require a response that asks all members of our community to uphold our shared values as outlined in the [Virginia Tech Principles of Community](https://www.inclusive.vt.edu/Programs/vtpoc0.html). Since incidents often fall beyond the reach of policy and laws, it is imperative that we respond as a unified community to denounce such behavior.

- [Student Affairs](https://students.vt.edu/) – Student Affairs professionals are committed to the holistic development of the Virginia Tech student experience, from orientation to graduation day. Students interact with Student Affairs staff from a variety of departments such as [Housing and Residence Life](https://housing.vt.edu/), [Dining Services](https://dining.vt.edu/), and [Student Engagement and Campus Life](https://campuslife.vt.edu/).

## Other Student Affairs Departments

- [Cook Counseling Center](https://ucc.vt.edu/)

- [Schiffert Health Center](https://healthcenter.vt.edu/)

- [Services for Students with Disabilities](https://ssd.vt.edu/)

chunks.title: Food Security | Dean of Students
chunks.text:
## Food Security

Photo credit: Darren Van Dyke

#### Nearly one in six Virginia Tech students is impacted by food insecurity. The Dean of Students office supports student success with resources and information to increase food access.

## Virginia Tech Food Access Programs

- [The Market of Virginia Tech](https://foodaccess.vt.edu/) is a university program available to all Virginia Tech students in need of food support. The Market is located just off campus and offers drop-in hours each week, students only need to bring a Hokie Passport to use The Market. Visit their website to learn more about each of their programs and view upcoming hours.

## Community Food Access Programs

- [209 Marketplace](https://www.209marketplace.com/) is a student-ran food pantry located just off campus. This program is open to any Virginia Tech student but does require a form for first-time customers. Visit their website to see up-to-date hours and location information.

- [The NRV Food Assistance Directory](https://cfnrv.org/thrive-food-access-network/) is an up-to-date resource that lists all food assistance resources available in the New River Valley.
